names.display_en: Liu Yuan, Founder of Han (Former Zhao)

summary: 乘八王之乱于离石起兵，称大单于、汉王，以绍汉为号召；永嘉二年称帝迁都平阳，为十六国割据开端之首，史称聪敏好学。
summary_en: Rising at Lishi amid the War of the Eight Princes, he styled himself Great Chanyu and King of Han in succession to the Han house; in the 2nd year of Yongjia he took the throne and moved his capital to Pingyang, opening the Sixteen States era — the histories praise his quickness and love of learning.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现胡汉混杂、英武有谋的开国之君之态，衣冠从匈奴汉国初制。属艺术想象。

timeline.summary_en: A Xiongnu of the Xinxing tribe, styled Yuanhai, descendant of Modu; studious from youth in the Mao Odes, the Jing-school Changes, and Sun–Wu military art.

timeline.summary_en: He took the imperial throne, styled the realm Han, moved the capital to Pingyang, and installed his officials.

timeline.title: 遣将寇洛阳
timeline.summary: 遣刘聪、王弥等攻洛阳不克，为日后陷洛铺垫。
timeline.summary_en: He sent Liu Cong, Wang Mi, and others against Luoyang without success — the prelude to its later fall.

timeline.title: 刘渊崩
timeline.summary: 崩于平阳，子和继，旋为聪所杀，聪自立。
timeline.summary_en: He died at Pingyang; his son He succeeded, was at once slain by Cong, and Cong took the throne.

timeline.title: 汉甥叙事
timeline.summary: 以汉甥、绍汉自居，争正统；史称聪敏好学。
timeline.summary_en: Claiming descent through a Han princess to continue the Han line, he contested legitimacy; the histories call him quick and studious.

bio_md:
# 汉（前赵）高祖 · 主要事迹

刘渊字元海，新兴匈奴人，冒顿之后。幼好学，习《毛诗》《京氏易》及孙吴兵法，「猿臂善射，膂力过人」。八王之乱起，刘渊乘乱于离石起兵，称大单于，旋称汉王，建元元熙——以「汉之甥」自居，尊刘禅为孝怀皇帝，立汉高祖以下三祖五宗神主而祭之，欲争华夏正统。十六国割据，自刘渊始。

永嘉二年，渊即皇帝位，国号汉，迁都平阳，署置百官；遣刘聪、王弥等攻洛阳不克，为日后陷洛之铺垫。然匈奴汉国之制，胡汉分治、军政混行，其政权之根基未固。永嘉四年，刘渊崩，谥光文皇帝。子和继立，旋为弟聪所杀，汉国之政归于刘聪。

刘渊以匈奴之裔，乘晋室之乱而建政权，首开「五胡乱华」之局。其以绍汉为号召、行汉家礼仪，可见汉文化之浸润已深；然其政权终以武功立、以暴政传，后嗣相残、民心不附，不过二十余年而国灭。渊之起兵，非为仁政，实为野心，史家于其「聪敏好学」之外，更见胡汉冲突之始。

> 参考：点校本《晋书》卷101《刘元海载记》、卷102《刘聪载记》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yuan, styled Yuanhai, was a Xiongnu of Xinxing, descended from Modu. Studious from youth, he mastered the Mao Odes, the Jing-school Changes, and the military art of Sun and Wu, "long of arm, a fine archer, of unusual strength." When the War of the Eight Princes broke out, he rose at Lishi, styled himself Great Chanyu, then King of Han — claiming descent through a Han princess, he honored Liu Shan as Emperor Xiaohuai and set up the ancestral tablets of the Han emperors to contest legitimacy with the Jin. The Sixteen States era begins with Liu Yuan.

In the 2nd year of Yongjia he took the imperial throne, styled the realm Han, moved his capital to Pingyang, and installed his officials; his lieutenants Liu Cong and Wang Mi attacked Luoyang without success — the prelude to its fall. But the Xiongnu Han state ran on a divided system of Hu and Han, arms and government mixed, and its foundations were never firm. In the 4th year of Yongjia Liu Yuan died, posthumously Guangwen. His son He succeeded and was at once slain by his brother Cong, and the state passed to Cong.

A Xiongnu who rode the Jin collapse to found a state, Liu Yuan opened the "Five Barbarian invasions." His claim of succession to Han and his adoption of Han rites show how deep Chinese culture had sunk into him; yet his state stood on arms and passed on tyranny — heirs murdering heirs, the people's hearts lost — and perished within a generation. His rising was ambition, not benevolence; the historians, beyond his "quickness and love of learning," see the beginning of the Hu–Han conflict.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 101 (records of Liu Yuanhai), ch. 102 (records of Liu Cong).
